newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks start lower on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: French stocks start lower on profit-taking.

text.p: French shares started lower on profit-taking on Thursday on the morning after the U.S. election party on Wednesday which fired the blue-chip index to a year high at a level last seen in 1994.
Weakness in bond prices on Thursday, as well as slippage in the dollar, prompted a round of consolidation, dealers said.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was down 16.57 points or 0.75 percent at 2,196.80 at 0914 GMT while the CAC-40 futures contract was down at 17 at 2,201.
On charts, first support for the index is seen at 2,195 and resistance at 2,225.
"It's more a movement of consolidation that a big decline. Support is seen at 2,192, then 2,187 and the trading range is seen at between 2,187 and 2,234," a dealer said.
The CAC-40 index reached a year high of 2,218.57 and a closing high of 2,213.37 on Wednesday. Its life high stands at 2,360.98, reached on February 2, 1994.
Zodiac up 1.9 percent, Labinal up 4.52 percent, Intertechnique up 2.53 percent, Thomson-CSF down 0.31 percent and Latecoere seen benefitting from USAir bumper order for 120 Airbus planes.
Elf down 1.01 percent in the wake of a U.K. refining and distribution merger with Chevron and Murco.
Roussel-Uclaf up 2.5 percent on renewed Hoechst buy-out talk.
